title: September 2019 Class College Final Exam (Part 5 of 6)
unit: Comprehensive Nursing (Medical-Surgical, Paediatrics, Midwifery, Community Health, Mental Health, Pharmacology, Research, Leadership and Management)

sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs from the September 2019 class College Final Exam paper (Kenya Registered Nursing, sat 18 November 2022, Multiple Choice Questions, Q81 to Q100).

questions.text: The QRS complex represents:
questions.explanation: Ventricular systole (B) is correct because the QRS complex on the ECG is the electrical depolarisation of the ventricles, which triggers ventricular contraction (systole). Atrial systole (A) is incorrect because atrial depolarisation produces the P wave, and the atrial repolarisation is hidden within the larger QRS complex. Only ventricular diastole (C) is incorrect because ventricular repolarisation, which comes before relaxation, is shown by the T wave, not the QRS. Both atrial and ventricular systole (D) is incorrect because the atria and the ventricles contract at different times, atria after the P wave and ventricles after the QRS.

questions.text: Manifestations of left sided heart failure include:

options.A: Distended jugular vein, dyspnea on exertion

questions.explanation: Orthopnea, hemoptysis (D) is correct because in left-sided failure the left ventricle cannot pump forward, so blood backs up into the lungs, causing pulmonary congestion: orthopnoea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea, cough, crackles, frothy or blood-stained sputum (haemoptysis) and fatigue. Distended jugular vein, dyspnea on exertion (A) is incorrect because a raised jugular venous pressure is a right-sided sign, although exertional dyspnoea is left-sided. Dependent edema, hepatosplenomegaly (B) is incorrect because both are right-sided signs from systemic venous congestion. Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, ascites (C) is incorrect because PND is left-sided but ascites is a right-sided sign.

questions.text: A possible diagnosis for Mr. V, a 65-year-old who is admitted with thickened and opaque nails, shiny, atrophic and dry skin with sparse hair growth is:
questions.explanation: Peripheral vascular disease (B) is correct because chronic arterial insufficiency reduces the blood supply to the limbs, causing thick brittle nails, shiny thin dry skin, hair loss, cool pale limbs, weak pulses and claudication. Venous thromboembolism (A) is incorrect because it presents with a swollen, warm, painful limb from a clot. Raynaud disease (C) is incorrect because it causes episodes of white, blue then red colour change of the fingers or toes triggered by cold or stress. Varicose veins (D) is incorrect because they are dilated twisted superficial veins with oedema, brown skin discolouration and venous ulcers, not hair loss and atrophic skin.

questions.text: Cardiomyopathy with increased diastolic and systolic pressure but decreased ejection fraction is:
questions.explanation: Dilated (D) is correct because in dilated cardiomyopathy the ventricles enlarge and the walls thin, so contractility falls (low ejection fraction) and the filling pressures and volumes in diastole and systole rise, leading to heart failure. Arrhythmogenic right ventricular (A) is incorrect because the right ventricle muscle is replaced by fat and fibrous tissue, mainly causing ventricular arrhythmias. Hypertrophic (B) is incorrect because the ventricular wall and septum thicken with a small cavity, and the ejection fraction is normal or high. Restrictive (C) is incorrect because the ventricles are stiff and fill poorly, with normal or near normal ejection fraction.

questions.text: Effects of shock on the cell include:
questions.explanation: Hypernatremia, lysosomal rupture (B) is the marked answer because when shock cuts oxygen supply the cell makes too little ATP and the sodium-potassium pump fails, so sodium (and water) builds up inside the cell, the cell swells, lysosomal membranes rupture and release enzymes that digest the cell. Hypokalemia, decrease membrane permeability (A) is incorrect because potassium leaks out of the cell and membrane permeability increases. Hyponatremia, cellular shrinkage (C) is incorrect because the cells swell instead of shrinking. Hyperkalemia, cellular edema (D) lists changes that also occur (potassium leaves the cell and the cell swells), so this item is contestable, but the key given on the paper is B.

questions.text: The appropriate health message following hemorrhoidectomy include:

options.A: Use prescribed pain medication before a bowel movement
options.B: Administer oil retention enema to empty colon
options.C: Eat a low fiber diet to rest the colon

questions.explanation: Use prescribed pain medication before a bowel movement (A) is correct because the first stools after hemorrhoidectomy are painful, and patients who fear pain hold back stool and become constipated, so analgesia is taken beforehand; sitz baths, a high-fibre diet, plenty of fluids and stool softeners are also advised. Administer oil retention enema to empty colon (B) is incorrect because enemas can injure the fresh surgical wound. Eat a low fiber diet to rest the colon (C) is incorrect because a low-fibre diet causes hard stools and straining, which damage the wound. Take mineral oil before bedtime (D) is incorrect because stool softeners and bulk-forming fibre are preferred, and regular mineral oil interferes with absorption of fat-soluble vitamins.

questions.text: Digested fats are primarily absorbed into the:
questions.explanation: Lacteals (D) is correct because digested fats (monoglycerides and fatty acids) are rebuilt into triglycerides inside the intestinal cells, packaged into chylomicrons, and enter the lacteals (lymph vessels in the centre of each villus), then pass through the thoracic duct into the blood. Central arterioles (A) is incorrect because villi contain a central lacteal, and absorption is not into arterioles. Lamina propria (B) is incorrect because it is the connective tissue core of the villus in which the lacteal lies, not the absorbing vessel. Villus capillaries (C) is incorrect because they absorb water-soluble nutrients such as glucose, amino acids and short-chain fatty acids.

questions.text: The main route of transmission of Hepatitis A is via:
questions.explanation: Feco-oral route (B) is correct because hepatitis A virus is passed in the stool and spread through contaminated food and water and poor hygiene, so prevention is by safe water, handwashing, proper sanitation and vaccination. Sexual contact (A) is incorrect because it is a main route for hepatitis B, although it can spread through oral-anal contact. IV drug use (C) is incorrect because it spreads hepatitis B and C through shared needles. Infected blood or body fluids (D) is incorrect because that is the typical route of hepatitis B, C and D.

questions.text: A risk factor for the development of a Hiatal hernia is:
questions.explanation: Weakness of diaphragmatic muscle (D) is correct because a hiatal hernia occurs when part of the stomach pushes up through the oesophageal hiatus of the diaphragm, and a weak or widened diaphragmatic opening (ageing, congenital) allows this; other risks are obesity, pregnancy, ascites and straining that raise intra-abdominal pressure. Increased intra-thoracic pressure (A) is incorrect because the pressure that pushes the stomach upward is raised intra-abdominal pressure, not intra-thoracic. Weakness of the esophageal muscles (B) is incorrect because the defect is in the diaphragm, not the oesophageal wall. Increased esophageal muscle pressure (C) is incorrect because it is not a recognised cause.

questions.text: A priority nursing care for a client with esophageal varices include:
questions.explanation: Recognizing hemorrhage (A) is correct because varices can rupture and cause life-threatening bleeding (haematemesis, melaena, tachycardia, falling blood pressure), so early recognition and quick action (airway, IV access, fluids, blood, and endoscopic or drug treatment) is the priority. Controlling blood pressure (B) is incorrect as the first priority because portal hypertension is managed with long-term beta-blockers, and in bleeding the aim is to restore volume, not to lower pressure. Encouraging nutritional intake (C) is incorrect because it is important but not urgent, and oral intake is withheld during bleeding. Teaching the client about varices (D) is incorrect because it is done once the patient is stable.

questions.text: The most common symptom associated with Adenomyosis is:
questions.explanation: Menorrhagia (B) is correct because in adenomyosis endometrial tissue grows into the uterine muscle, making the uterus enlarged and boggy, and the commonest symptoms are heavy prolonged menstrual bleeding and painful periods. Infertility (A) is incorrect because it is less common and has other causes. Dyspareunia (C) is incorrect because it occurs in some women but is not the commonest symptom. Metrorrhagia (D) is incorrect because it is bleeding between periods, which is less typical than heavy periods.

questions.text: The following is thought to be a protective measure against Cervical cancer:
questions.explanation: Long term sexual abstinence (A) is correct because cervical cancer is strongly linked to persistent human papillomavirus (types 16 and 18) infection, which is sexually transmitted, so avoiding or delaying sexual contact lowers the risk; HPV vaccination, condom use and regular screening also protect. Oral contraceptive use (B) is incorrect because long-term use is associated with a slightly higher risk. Long term steroid use (C) is incorrect because it suppresses immunity and increases the risk of persistent HPV infection. Smoking (D) is incorrect because tobacco by-products damage cervical cells and raise the risk.

questions.text: Functional ovarian cysts include:
questions.explanation: Follicular cysts (B) is correct because functional cysts arise from the normal ovulation cycle: a follicular cyst forms when the follicle does not rupture, and a corpus luteum cyst forms after ovulation; they are usually harmless and resolve on their own in one to three cycles. Endometriosis (A) is incorrect because it is a disease in which endometrial tissue grows outside the uterus (it can form endometriomas), which is not a functional cyst. Dermoid cysts (C) is incorrect because they are benign germ cell tumours (mature teratomas) containing hair and fat. Fibromas (D) is incorrect because they are solid benign tumours of ovarian connective tissue.

questions.text: Physiological jaundice:
questions.explanation: Polycythemia is a predisposing factor (D) is correct because the newborn has a high red cell mass with shorter-lived red cells, so more bilirubin is made, and the immature liver cannot conjugate it quickly enough, so polycythaemia increases the risk of physiological jaundice. Affects premature neonates only (A) is incorrect because it also affects term babies, though it is more marked and lasts longer in preterm babies. Appears within 12-24 hours of birth (B) is incorrect because physiological jaundice appears after 24 hours (usually day 2 to 3), and jaundice in the first 24 hours is pathological. Is caused by ABO incompatibility (C) is incorrect because that is haemolytic disease of the newborn, a pathological jaundice.

questions.text: In the fetal circulation, the blood vessel from the umbilical vein to the inferior vena cava which carries oxygenated blood to the heart is:
questions.explanation: Ductus venosus (B) is correct because it is the fetal shunt that lets most of the oxygen-rich blood from the umbilical vein bypass the liver and flow directly into the inferior vena cava toward the right atrium. Ductus arteriosus (A) is incorrect because it links the pulmonary artery to the aorta, bypassing the lungs. Foramen ovale (C) is incorrect because it is the opening between the right and left atria. Hypogastric arteries (D) is incorrect because they continue as the umbilical arteries, which carry deoxygenated blood from the fetus to the placenta.

questions.text: Eight hours post lumbar puncture, the patient reports severe headache. The nurse advises the patient to:
questions.explanation: Take lots of water (D) is the marked answer because the headache after lumbar puncture is caused by leakage of cerebrospinal fluid at the puncture site, and generous fluids (with analgesics and sometimes caffeine) help the body replace CSF; an epidural blood patch is used if it persists. Watch a favorite program (A) is incorrect because it does not treat the cause and keeps the patient upright. Lie supine in the bed (B) is also a standard supportive measure (lying flat eases the headache), so this item is contestable, but the key given is D. Walk around the ward (C) is incorrect because being upright increases the CSF pressure drop and worsens the headache.

questions.text: The following indicates secondary brain injury:

options.A: Fracture of the occipital bone, epidural hematoma

questions.explanation: Cerebral edema, increased intracranial pressure (B) is correct because secondary brain injury is the damage that develops hours to days after the impact, from swelling, raised intracranial pressure, hypoxia, low blood pressure and reduced cerebral perfusion. Fracture of the occipital bone, epidural hematoma (A) is incorrect because both are primary injuries that occur at the moment of impact. Raccoon's eye, intracerebral edema (C) is incorrect because raccoon's eyes are a sign of a basal skull fracture (a primary injury), even though oedema is secondary. Hallo sign, intracerebral edema (D) is incorrect because the halo sign (a ring of clear fluid around blood) indicates a CSF leak from a basal skull fracture, a primary injury.

questions.text: Vaccines that shouldn't be exposed to sunlight include:
questions.explanation: BCG, Measles (C) is correct because these freeze-dried vaccines are sensitive to light as well as heat, so the vials are kept in their cartons, protected from direct sunlight, and discarded within 6 hours of reconstitution. Pneumococcal and Measles (A) is incorrect because the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine is a liquid vaccine that is damaged by freezing rather than by light. Polio and Yellow fever (B) is incorrect because oral polio vaccine is the most heat-sensitive vaccine, and the yellow fever vaccine is mainly heat-sensitive. BCG, Polio (D) is incorrect because the polio vaccine is mainly heat-sensitive.

questions.text: Mrs. LL is a pastor's wife but she also practices witchcraft. What aspect of the role does she play:
questions.explanation: Role conflict (C) is correct because the expectations of the two roles are incompatible, since being a pastor's wife requires Christian values and practice, while practising witchcraft opposes them, so meeting one role's demands makes it impossible to meet the other's. Role multiplicity (A) is incorrect because it means holding many roles at the same time, which does not by itself imply conflict. Role confusion (B) is incorrect because it means the person is unsure what a role requires. Role strain (D) is incorrect because it is stress from being unable to meet the demands of a role, often from overload.

questions.text: Katayama syndrome is a manifestation in:
questions.explanation: Schistosomiasis (A) is correct because Katayama syndrome (acute schistosomiasis) is a hypersensitivity reaction 2 to 8 weeks after first exposure to the cercariae, as the worms mature and begin to lay eggs, with fever, cough, rash or urticaria, muscle pain, abdominal pain, eosinophilia and sometimes an enlarged liver and spleen. Onchocerciasis (B) is incorrect because it presents with itchy skin, nodules and eye disease (river blindness). Leishmaniasis (C) is incorrect because visceral disease (kala-azar) causes prolonged fever, weight loss, anaemia and a large spleen. Dracunculosis (D) is incorrect because the guinea worm causes a painful blister and ulcer through which the female worm emerges.
